about: The providers' own agent tools (CLIs, MCP servers, plugins and skills) that Homie's skills use or offer, and what stays Homie's. Nothing here installs by itself: a skill names its providers in its SKILL.md metadata, offers their tools only when the person wants that feature, and the person approves every install and signs in on the provider's own page. plugin.json points here (extensions.rocks.homie.providers); test/providers.test.mjs keeps this file, the skills and the Homie mod's guards in step.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
cloudflare.account: the studio's own Cloudflare account (the free Workers plan, no payment method)

cli.name: wrangler
cli.install: the studio's own pinned copy, installed with the studio (npx wrangler in the studio folder)
cli.signIn: npx wrangler login (opens Cloudflare in the browser; --device prints a code to approve on any device when no browser can open here)
cli.homieUses: whoami --json, deploy, d1 create, d1 migrations apply --remote, r2 bucket create, r2 object put and get --remote, secret put (from a page on this computer, never the chat), ai models list --json

plugin.brings: Cloudflare's own skills (cloudflare, wrangler, workers-best-practices, durable-objects, agents-sdk and more) and its API MCP server

mcp.name: cloudflare-docs
mcp.use: Cloudflare's current docs (limits, Wrangler flags, Workers AI models) instead of memory

mcp.name: cloudflare
mcp.use: the whole Cloudflare API (search, execute): reading the account; the studio's own resources change only through its deploy

mcp.name: cloudflare-bindings
mcp.use: listing Workers, D1, R2 and KV (the claude.ai Cloudflare Developer Platform connector is this server)

mcp.name: cloudflare-observability
mcp.use: a live Worker's logs and errors

homieKeeps: the studio's own Worker, D1 database, R2 bucket and secrets are created, changed and deleted only by npm run deploy and homie-studio, which record what they create in studio.json and never touch what they did not create
the free plan: no payment method, R2 only when the person adds storage
secrets go from a page on this computer straight to wrangler secret put, never through the chat
the Workers AI model probe and the AI guides' daily budget

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.account: the creator's own ElevenLabs account and plan

cli.name: elevenlabs
cli.signIn: elevenlabs auth login (opens ElevenLabs in the browser; the sign-in stays in the OS keychain)
cli.homieUses: auth status, user subscription get, music compose_detailed (with --dry-run first), speech-to-text convert, music separate_stems

plugin.brings: ElevenLabs' own skills (music, sound effects, text to speech, speech to text and more) and its hosted MCP server

mcp.name: elevenlabs
mcp.use: speech, voices, transcription and agents; it has no music tools, so songs go through the CLI here

homieKeeps: the plan, the credits left and the rights that plan gives, said before anything is made
a cap the person agreed to, a dry run first, the cost read off the account before and after, a receipt per render, never the same paid request twice
the composition plan for anything sung and the check that every line was sung
the song pages and the RIGHTS notes

fal.name: fal

cli.name: fal
cli.signIn: fal auth login (opens fal in the browser); fal keys create --scope API makes the key the skills read as FAL_KEY
cli.homieUses: none: the skills call fal's documented queue and pricing APIs themselves, so every paid call is priced, capped, receipted and resumable

fal.skillsOnly: https://github.com/fal-ai-community/skills (installed by fal's genmedia CLI: genmedia init)

mcp.name: fal
mcp.use: finding models, reading their input schemas and prices (search_models, recommend_model, get_model_schema, get_pricing, search_docs); paid runs go through the skills' scripts, never its run_model or submit_job

homieKeeps: the price read from fal's own pricing API before every call, a cap the person agreed to, a receipt the moment fal accepts a job, and a resume that never pays twice
the derived style prompt and the golden images every prompt starts from
the checks (does a texture tile, is it small enough for a phone, does a cover promise only what the game holds) and the RIGHTS notes

tripo.name: Tripo
tripo.account: the creator's own fal account (Tripo's models run on fal)

cli.name: tripo
cli.homieUses: none: generated props use Tripo's models on fal (tripo3d/p1/image-to-3d), where fal's terms and receipts apply

homieKeeps: Tripo on fal only, until Tripo's own terms for what it makes have been read and recorded in the models skill's RIGHTS notes
the concept in the game's locked style first, then the mesh, optimised to the phone budgets and recorded with its licence

github.name: GitHub
github.account: the creator's own GitHub account (optional: a private backup and publishing by pull request)

cli.name: gh
cli.install: brew install gh (or the GitHub CLI's own installer)
cli.signIn: gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web (a one-time code typed at github.com/login/device)

plugin.brings: GitHub's MCP server (it reads a personal access token from GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; the gh sign-in needs none)

mcp.name: github
mcp.use: issues, pull requests and Actions runs, when the person wants them; /readonly reads only

homieKeeps: the sign-in through GitHub's own device page, never a token pasted into the chat
a pull request the person merges in GitHub: Homie never merges it for them

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.account: the studio's own Stripe account (the shop's: a sandbox first, live only when the owner says the shop is ready), and for Stripe Projects the creator's own Stripe sign-in

cli.name: stripe
cli.signIn: stripe agent setup (it installs Stripe's agent plugin, whose MCP server signs in on Stripe's own consent page); Stripe Projects signs in with stripe projects init. The shop never uses the CLI's own login to touch an account
cli.homieUses: agent setup; and for setup --via stripe-projects (a prototype; 1.40.0 or later with the projects plugin): projects status, search, add (free plans, never --confirm-paid-service), link, env --json (names only), env show, env --pull

plugin.setup: npm install -g @stripe/cli@latest && stripe agent setup (it finds Claude Code, Codex and others, and installs the plugin for each)
plugin.brings: Stripe's MCP server and Stripe's own skills (stripe-best-practices, stripe-docs, stripe-projects and more), kept up to date

mcp.name: stripe
mcp.use: the shop's catalog (shop catalog lists the writes), tax settings and registrations, and how sales are, read-only; the claude.ai Stripe connector is this server. Never a webhook endpoint or an API key through it (the mod refuses a write that would hand back a signing secret); refunds and money going out wait for Stripe's own confirmation link. From 2026-10-31 it takes only OAuth or Agent-tagged keys

projects.what: Stripe Projects: Stripe's CLI plugin that makes or links provider accounts (Cloudflare, ElevenLabs and more) on the creator's own Stripe sign-in, and syncs their credentials to the project's git-ignored .env

homieKeeps: the shop's money rules: the studio's own Stripe, shop.json's checked prices, the kids rules and the monthly cap; homie.rocks never holds money

one restricted key the owner makes in Stripe's Dashboard and pastes on a page on their own computer, straight to the Worker secret; the webhook made there with it, its signing secret never in the chat
refunds are the owner's one tap; Stripe's own confirmation link for anything Stripe holds
Stripe Projects on free plans only: no payment method, no paid tier, never a credential's value in output
